metadata.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Linear Convolutional Networks

nodes.name: Linear fully connected network
nodes.statement: \textbf{Linear fully connected network}\quad In a fully connected linear network, the nodes between successive layers $l-1$ and $l$ are densely connected with edge weights $\u_l\in\bR^{D_{l-1}\times D_l}$, and all the weights are independent parameters. This model class is parameterized by $\u=[\u_l]_{l=1}^L\in\prod_{l=1}^L \bR^{D_{l-1}\times D_l}$ and the computation for intermediate nodes $\h_l$ and the composite linear map $f_{\u}(\x)$ is given by, \begin{equation} \h_l=\u_l^\top\h_{l-1}\quad \tand \quad f_{\u}(\x)=\h_L=\u_L^\top\u_{L-1}^\top\ldots\u_1^\top\x. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Linear convolutional network
nodes.statement: \textbf{Linear convolutional network}\quad We consider one-dimensional convolutional network architectures where each non-output layer has exactly $D$ units (same as the input dimensionality) and the linear transformations from layer ${l-1}$ to layer $l$ are given by the following circular convolutional operation\footnote{We follow the convention used in neural networks literature that refer to the operation in \eqref{eq:conv} as convolution, while in the signal processing terminology, \eqref{eq:conv} is known as the discrete circular cross-correlation operator} parameterized by full width filters with weights $[\u_l\in\bR^D]_{l=1}^{L-1}$. For $l=1,2,\ldots,L-1$, \begin{equation} \quad\h_l[d]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{D}}\sum_{k=0}^{D-1}\u_l[k]\,\h_{l-1}\left[(d+k)\text{ mod } D\right]:=\left(\h_{l-1}\star \u_l\right)[d]. \end{equation} The output layer is fully connected and parameterized by weights $\u_L \in \bR^D$. The parameters of the model class therefor consists of $L$ vectors of size $D$ collectively denoted by ${\u=[\u_l]_{l=1}^{L}\in\prod_{l=1}^L \bR^{D}}$, and the composite linear map $f_{\u}(\x)$ is given by: \begin{equation} f_{\u}(\x)=\left((((\x\star\u_1)\star\u_2)\ldots)\star\u_{L-1}\right)^\top \u_L. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Parameterization mapping $\P:\c{W}\to\bR^D$ ($\P_{full}$, $\P_{conv}$)
nodes.statement: The fully connected and convolutional linear networks described above can both be represented in terms of a mapping $\P:\c{W}\to\bR^D$ that maps the input parameters $\u\in\c{W}$ to a linear predictor in $\bR^D$, such that the output of the network is given by $f_{\u}({\x})=\innerprod{\x}{\P(\u)}$. For fully connected networks, the mapping is given by $\P_{full}(\u)=\u_1\u_{2}\ldots\u_L$, and for convolutional networks, $\P_{conv}(\u)=\left(\big((\u_L^{\downarrow}\star\u_{L-1})\star\u_{L-2}\big)\ldots\star\u_{1}\right)^{\downarrow}$, where $\u^{\downarrow}$ denotes the flipped vector corresponding to $\u$, given by ${\u}^{\downarrow}[k]=\u{[D-k-1]}$ for $k=0,1,\ldots,D-1$.

nodes.name: Homogeneous Polynomial
nodes.statement: A multivariate polynomial function $\P:\bR^P\to \bR^D$ is said to be homogeneous, if for some finite integer $\nu<\infty$, $\forall \alpha\in\bR,\mathbf{v}\in\bR^P$, $\P(\alpha \mathbf{v})=\alpha^\nu \P(\mathbf{v})$.

nodes.name: Empirical risk minimization $\c{L}_{\P}(\u)$ for a linear network
nodes.statement: \textbf{Separable linear classification}\quad Consider a binary classification dataset $\{(\x_{n},y_{n}):n=1,2,\ldots N\}$ with $\x_n\in\bR^D$ and $y_n\in\{-1,1\}$. The empirical risk minimization objective for training a linear network parameterized as $\P(\u)$ is given as follows, \begin{equation} \min_{\u\in\c{W}}\;\c{L}_{\P}(\u) := \sum_{n=1}^{N} \ell(\innerprod{\x_n}{\P(\u)},y_n), \end{equation} where $\ell:\bR\times \{-1,1\}\to\bR_+$ is some surrogate loss for classification accuracy, \eg logistic loss $\ell(\hat{y},y)=\log(1+\exp(-\hat{y}y))$ and exponential loss $\ell(\hat{y},y)= \exp(-\hat{y}y)$.

Remark on circular convolution and full-width filters
nodes.statement: \textit{Remark: }We use circular convolution with a scaling of $\nicefrac{1}{\sqrt{D}}$ to make the analysis cleaner. For convolutions with zero-padding, we expect a similar behavior. Secondly, since our goal here to study implicit bias in sufficiently over-parameterized models, we only study full dimensional convolutional filters. In practice it is common to have filters of width $K$ smaller than the number of input features, which can change the implicit bias.

nodes.statement: \citet{soudry2017implicit} studied this implicit bias of gradient descent on \eqref{eq:lm} over the direct parameterization of $\w$. nodes.name: Stolz--Cesaro theorem
nodes.statement: Assume that $\{a_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ and $\{b_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ are two sequences of real numbers such that $\{b_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ is strictly monotonic and diverging (i.e., monotone increasing with $b_k\to\infty$, or monotone decreasing with $b_k\to-\infty$). eq0$, we have $ ar{\gamma}|\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]|\le ar{\gamma}|\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d']|$. Moreover from eq.\eqref{eq:cn-slackness-mag}), we know that $ ar{\gamma}|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d']|=1$ for all $d'$ with $\hat{ ar{\w}}^\infty[d']

icefrac{1}{(1+x)}\ge (1-x)$ for $x< 1$ since $\eta_tp(t)\left(|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]|+| delta[t]_d|ight)< 0.5$ for all $t\ge t_1$, and in $(c)$, we absorbed all $o(p(t))$ terms as $ delta^{(t)}_{d,d'}p(t)$ for $ delta^{(t)}_{d,d'}	o0$ and used $|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]|-|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d']|=2\epsilon>0$. From eq. \eqref{eq:cn-ud++}, we have that for all $d$, \[| {u}^{(t+1)}_d|\le(1+\mu\eta_t p(t))| {u}^{(t)}_d|\le | {u}^{(t_0)}_d|\prod_{u=t_0}^t(1+\mu \eta_up(u))\le | {u}^{(t_0)}_d|\exp(\sum_{u=t_0}^t\mu\eta_u p(u)).\] Moreover, we have $ {u}^{(t)}_d	o\infty$ for at least one $d$, and for any finite step sizes and finite $t_0$, $| {u}^{(t_0)}_d|<\infty$. Thus, for any $\epsilon>0$, we also have $\prod_{u=t_0}^t(1+\epsilon \eta_up(u))\ge \epsilon\sum_{u=t_0}^t \eta_u p(u)	o\infty$. \end{proof} From eq. \eqref{eq:prodk} and above claim, we conclude that for all $d,d'$, if $|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]|>|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d']|$, then $\kappa_{d,d'}^{(t)}	o\infty$. \end{asparaenum}

This along with eq. \eqref{eq:tdud} gives us $ rac{ oldsymbol{	au}_d^{(t)}}{ {u}_d^{(t)}}	o0$. Moreover, since $|\hat\w^{(t)}[d]|	o\infty$, we have $|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|$ or $|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|	o\infty$. Further, using $\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}	o1$, we have $| {u}_d^{(t)}|=|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|+|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}	o\infty$. We now only need to show that these results also hold for $d$ such that $\hat{ ar\w}^\infty[d]=0$. Recall from the assumptions of the theorem that even when $\hat{ ar\w}^\infty[d]=0$, $\exists \phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^\infty[d]}\in[0,2\pi)$ such that $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}	o\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^\infty[d]}}$. We now prove the lemma by showing the following steps for $d$ such that $\hat{ ar\w}^\infty[d]=0$. :  egin{compactenum}[Step 1.] \item Show $ rac{|{\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]}|}{|{\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]}|}	o1$. \item Show $	ext{Re}(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]}})=2\cos(\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}-\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]})\ge 0$. \end{compactenum} \paragraph{Proof of lemma assuming Step 1 and Step 2 hold} The above steps would imply that in eq. \eqref{eq:tdud},  egin{compactitem} \item the denominator satisfies  egin{equation}  egin{split} \left|1+ rac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}ight|	o&\left|1+\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]}}ight|\ &\ge \left|1+	ext{Re}(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^\infty[d]}})ight|\ge1. \end{split} \end{equation} \item the numerator satisfies  egin{equation} \left| delta^{(t)}_{2,d}\left(1- rac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}ight)ight|\le | delta^{(t)}_{2,d}|\left|1+ rac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}ight|	o0. \end{equation} \end{compactitem} These eqs. along with eq. \eqref{eq:tdud} in turn prove the lemma, 	extit{i.e.}, $ rac{ oldsymbol{	au}_d^{(t)}}{ {u}_d^{(t)}}	o0$ and $| {u}_d^{(t)}|	o\infty$. \paragraph{Showing Step 1 and Step 2}  egin{asparaenum}[	extbf{Step} 1.] \item 	extit{Show $ rac{|{\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]}|}{|{\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]}|}	o1$.} From the dynamics of $\hat{\u}^{(t)}_l[d]$ from eq. \eqref{eq:cn-grad-2}, we have the following,  egin{equation}  egin{split} |\hat{\u}^{(t+1)}_1[d]|^2&=|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2+\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]\cdot\hat{\w}^{(t)*}[d]+\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)*}[d]\cdot\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]+\eta_t^2|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2\ |\hat{\u}^{(t+1)}_2[d]|^2&=|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2+\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]\cdot\hat{\w}^{(t)*}[d]+\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)*}[d]\cdot\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]+\eta_t^2|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2 \end{split} \end{equation} Note that since $|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2	o0$ and $\eta_t$ are finite, we have that $\exists t_1$ such that for all $t\ge t_1$, $\eta_t|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2\le1$. From the above equation, we have the following for $t\ge t_1$,  egin{equation}  egin{split} \left||\hat{\u}^{(t+1)}_1[d]|^2-|\hat{\u}^{(t+1)}_2[d]|^2ight|&=\left|\left(1-\eta_t^2|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2ight)\left(|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2-\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2ight)ight|\ &\overset{(a)}{=}\left(\prod_{u=t_1}^t\left(1-\eta_u^2|\hat{\z}^{(u)}[d]|^2ight)ight)\left||\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_1[d]|^2-\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_2[d]|^2ight|\ &\le \left||\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_1[d]|^2-\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_2[d]|^2ight|<\infty, \end{split} \end{equation} where $(a)$ follows from iterating over $t$ and using $|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2\le1$ for $t\ge t_1$. Since $|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|=|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|\cdot|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|	o\infty$, at least one of $|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|,|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|$ must diverge. Without loss of generality, let $|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|	o\infty$. Let $c(t):=|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2-|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2$ with $|c(t)|<\infty$. We have  egin{equation}  rac{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2}{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2}=1+ rac{c(t)}{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2}\overset{(a)}	o 1, \end{equation} where the convergence in $(a)$ follows since $|c(t)|<\infty$ (from eq. \eqref{eq:cn-ulnorm}) and $|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|	o\infty$. \item 	extit{Show $	ext{Re}(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]}})=2\cos(\phi_{\hat{ ar\z}^\infty[d]}-\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]})\ge 0$.} Note that from Step 1 above, we have that $ rac{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2}{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2}	o1$, which implies $ rac{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2+|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2}{2|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|}= rac{|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2+|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2}{2|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|\cdot|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|}	o 1$. Thus, there exists $ delta[t]_{1,d}	o0$, such that  egin{equation} |\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2+|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2=2|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|\cdot(1+ delta[t]_{1,d}). \end{equation} Also, from eq. \eqref{eq:cn-z}, there exists $ delta[t]_{2,d}	o0$, such that  egin{equation} \hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]=\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d] p(t)+ delta[t]_{2,d}p(t)	ext{, with }p(t)=
orm{\hat{\z}^{(t)}}	o 0. \end{equation} Using the above representations, along with eq. \eqref{eq:cn-grad-2}, we have the following,  egin{align} 
onumber\hat{\w}^{(t+1)}[d]&=\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]+\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]\left[|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2+|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2+\eta_t{\hat{\z}^{(t)}}[d]\cdot\hat{\w}^{(t)*}[d]ight]\ 
onumber&\overset{(a)}=\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]+2\eta_tp(t)|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|\left(\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d] + delta[t]_{2,d}ight)\left[1+ delta[t]_{1,d}+
icefrac{1}{2}\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}ight]\%\left[1+ delta[t]_{1,d}ight]\ &\overset{(b)}{:=}\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]+2\eta_tp(t)|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|\left[\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d] + delta[t]_{3,d}ight], \end{align} where $(a)$ follows from substituting eqs. \eqref{eq:cnt3}-\eqref{eq:cnt4}, and $(b)$ follows from using $|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|\le p(t)	o0$ and defining $ delta[t]_{3,d}= delta[t]_{2,d}\left[1+ delta[t]_{1,d}+
icefrac{1}{2}\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}ight]+\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]\left[ delta[t]_{1,d}+
icefrac{1}{2}\eta_t\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}ight]	o0$. Denote $\Delta_d=\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]}-\phi_{\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]}$. Additionally, from the assumption in the theorem, we have $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}	o\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar\w}^{\infty}[d]}}$, hence there exists $ delta[t]_{4,d}	o0$ such that $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]}}=\e^{\ci\Delta_d}(1+ delta[t]_{4,d})$. onumber|\hat{\w}^{(t+1)}[d]|^2&=|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|^2 igg(\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}+2\eta_tp(t)\left[\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d] + delta[t]_{3,d}ight] igg) igg(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}+2\eta_tp(t)\left[\hat{ ar{\z}}^{\infty*}[d] + oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)*}_{3,d}ight] igg)\

onumber&\overset{(b)}{=}|\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]|^2\left[1+4\eta_tp(t)\left(|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]|\cos(\Delta_d) + delta[t]_{6,d}ight)ight]\ 
onumber&\overset{(c)}=|\hat{\w}^{(t_0)}[d]|^2\left[\prod_{u=t_0}^t \left(1+4\eta_up(u)\left(|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]|\cos(\Delta_d) + delta[u]_{6,d}ight)ight)ight]\ &\overset{(d)}\le |\hat{\w}^{(t_0)}[d]|^2\exp(\sum_{u=t_0}^t4\eta_up(u)\left(|\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]|\cos(\Delta_d) + delta[u]_{6,d}ight)), \end{align} where in $(a)$ we used $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}-\ci\phi_{\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]}}=\e^{\ci\Delta_d}(1+ delta[t]_{4,d})$ and collected all $o(p(t))$ terms into $ delta[t]_{5,d}=
icefrac{1}{2}\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}} oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)*}_{3,d}+2p(t)\hat{ ar{\z}}^\infty[d]\left[\hat{ ar{\z}}^{\infty*}[d] + oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)*}_{3,d}ight]+ delta[t]_{3,d} igg(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}+2p(t)\left[\hat{ ar{\z}}^{\infty*}[d] + oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)*}_{3,d}ight] igg)	o0$ (since $p(t), oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)}_{3,d}	o0$); in $(b)$ we defined $ delta[t]_{6,d}=
icefrac{1}{2} oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)*}_{4,d}\e^{\ci\Delta_d}+
icefrac{1}{2} oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)}_{3,d}\e^{-\ci\Delta_d}+ oldsymbol{\delta}^{(t)}_{5,d}	o0$; $(c)$ is obtained by iterating over $t$; and $(d)$ follows from using $(1+x)\le \exp(x)$. If possible, let $\cos(\Delta_d)=-2\epsilon<0$. nodes.statement: Recalling $\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}$ from eq. \eqref{eq:cn-ud+} and $\b{u}_d^{(t)}$ from eq. \eqref{eq:cn-ud}, we have the following: \begin{equation} \frac{\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}}{\b{u}_d^{(t)}}=\ci\bdelta^{(t)}_{2,d}\frac{ {\hat\u}_2^{(t)*}[d]-{\hat\u}_1^{(t)}[d]\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}}}{\hat{\u}_1^{(t)}[d]\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}}+\hat{\u}_2^{(t)*}[d].}=\ci\bdelta^{(t)}_{2,d}\frac{1-\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}}{1+\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}} \end{equation} For all $d$ if $\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]=\hat{\bar\u}_1^\infty[d]\cdot\hat{\bar\u}_2^\infty[d]\neq0$, the it is straightforward to see that $\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}=\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|/g(t)}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|/g(t)}\to\frac{|\hat{\bar\u}_1^{\infty}[d]|}{|\hat{\bar\u}_2^{\infty}[d]|}=1$ (from eq. \eqref{eq:cnt1}), and also that $\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\to\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]}}=1$ (from eq. \eqref{eq:cnt2}). This along with eq. \eqref{eq:tdud} gives us $\frac{\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}}{\b{u}_d^{(t)}}\to0$. Moreover, since $|\hat\w^{(t)}[d]|\to\infty$, we have $|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|$ or $|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|\to\infty$. Further, using $\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\to1$, we have $|\b{u}_d^{(t)}|=|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|+|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\to\infty$. We now only need to show that these results also hold for $d$ such that $\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]=0$. Recall from the assumptions of the theorem that even when $\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]=0$, $\exists \phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]}\in[0,2\pi)$ such that $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\to\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]}}$. We now prove the lemma by showing the following steps for $d$ such that $\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]=0$. : \begin{compactenum}[Step 1.] \item Show $\frac{|{\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]}|}{|{\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]}|}\to1$. \item Show $\text{Re}(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^{\infty}[d]}})=2\cos(\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}-\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^{\infty}[d]})\ge 0$. \end{compactenum}

nodes.name: Prove the lemma assuming Step 1 and Step 2
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Proof of lemma assuming Step 1 and Step 2 hold} The above steps would imply that in eq. \eqref{eq:tdud}, \begin{compactitem} \item the denominator satisfies \begin{equation} \begin{split} \left|1+\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\right|\to&\left|1+\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^{\infty}[d]}}\right|\\ &\ge \left|1+\text{Re}(\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]}})\right|\ge1. \end{split} \end{equation} \item the numerator satisfies \begin{equation} \left|\bdelta^{(t)}_{2,d}\left(1-\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\cdot\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}+\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\right)\right|\le |\bdelta^{(t)}_{2,d}|\left|1+\frac{|\hat\u_1^{(t)}[d]|}{|\hat\u_2^{(t)}[d]|}\right|\to0. \end{equation} \end{compactitem} These eqs. along with eq. \eqref{eq:tdud} in turn prove the lemma, \textit{i.e.}, $\frac{\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}}{\b{u}_d^{(t)}}\to0$ and $|\b{u}_d^{(t)}|\to\infty$.

From the above equation, we have the following for $t\ge t_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \left||\hat{\u}^{(t+1)}_1[d]|^2-|\hat{\u}^{(t+1)}_2[d]|^2\right|&=\left|\left(1-\eta_t^2|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2\right)\left(|\hat{\u}^{(t)}_1[d]|^2-\hat{\u}^{(t)}_2[d]|^2\right)\right|\\ &\overset{(a)}{=}\left(\prod_{u=t_1}^t\left(1-\eta_u^2|\hat{\z}^{(u)}[d]|^2\right)\right)\left||\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_1[d]|^2-\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_2[d]|^2\right|\\ &\le \left||\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_1[d]|^2-\hat{\u}^{(t_1)}_2[d]|^2\right|<\infty, \end{split} \end{equation} where $(a)$ follows from iterating over $t$ and using $|\hat{\z}^{(t)}[d]|^2\le1$ for $t\ge t_1$.
